item.title: Qila residents face 2km journey for water as creek levels remain low
item.description: Qila resident and Water Committee Secretary Jitendra Naidu says recent rain has improved the situation, with the community’s reservoir now about half full and supplying residents. However, he says the creek that feeds the community’s water system remains low, and they will continue to closely monitor it.
item.content:encoded:
Qila resident and Water Committee Secretary Jitendra Naidu says recent rain has improved the situation, with the community’s reservoir now about half full and supplying residents.

However, he says the creek that feeds the community’s water system remains low, and they will continue to closely monitor it.

Naidu says Qila is located high in the mountains and residents rely mainly on their community water system, which channels water from a creek into a catchment and reservoir.

He says if the main water source drops too low, residents may have to travel about two kilometres downhill to access another source.

Naidu says farmers are also feeling the effects of the dry weather, with some using 200-litre drums to collect whatever water they can from nearby creeks.

He says the community has not received water assistance during previous shortages, with residents largely relying on water sources available around them.

Naidu says he will continue checking the main water source as the community hopes for more rain.

Questions have been sent to the Ministry of Disaster Management regarding possible assistance for the community, however, there has been no response so far.

fijivillage News is continuing to seek a response.

item.title: Late Agni Deo Singh's parliamentary seat to remain vacant until the next general election
item.description: They wish to clarify the constitutional position regarding the resulting vacancy in the membership of Parliament. The Commission says under section 64(1) of the Constitution of the Republic of Fiji, the Electoral Commission is ordinarily responsible for awarding a vacant parliamentary seat held by a member of a political party to the highest-ranked available candidate of the same political party f
item.content:encoded:
They wish to clarify the constitutional position regarding the resulting vacancy in the membership of Parliament.

The Commission says under section 64(1) of the Constitution of the Republic of Fiji, the Electoral Commission is ordinarily responsible for awarding a vacant parliamentary seat held by a member of a political party to the highest-ranked available candidate of the same political party from the most recent General Election.

They say section 64(3) of the Constitution expressly provides that where a seat becomes vacant more than three years and six months after the first meeting of Parliament following the most recent General Election, the seat shall remain vacant until the next General Election.

The Commision says the constitutional period specified under section 64(3) elapsed on 24 June 2026.

The Electoral Commission will therefore not undertake any process to award the vacant seat to another candidate.

The Electoral Commission issues this clarification in the interest of ensuring that the constitutional process relating to vacancies in the membership of Parliament is clearly understood.

item.title: Police investigating assault captured on CCTV inside hair salon
item.description: Police are investigating an assault involving a man and a woman inside a hair salon, which was captured on CCTV. A video circulating online shows the man assaulting the woman inside the salon.
item.content:encoded:
Police are investigating an assault involving a man and a woman inside a hair salon, which was captured on CCTV.

A video circulating online shows the man assaulting the woman inside the salon.

CCTV footage shows the incident occurred on the 2nd of this month.

Police say they are yet to determine the location of the incident and are continuing to establish the circumstances surrounding the assault.

Police are advising the public that anyone with information should call 1681.

item.title: SCC, FRA and Waterways to meet next week over persistent flooding behind MHCC
item.description: We will meet again with the Fiji Roads Authority, and Ministry of Waterways next week to determine a permanent solution to the persistent flooding behind MHCC in Suva. This has been highlighted by Suva City Council CEO Tevita Boseiwaqa after fijivillage News raised concerns about the flooding that has again occurred behind MHCC this afternoon.
item.content:encoded:
We will meet again with the Fiji Roads Authority, and Ministry of Waterways next week to determine a permanent solution to the persistent flooding behind MHCC in Suva.

This has been highlighted by Suva City Council CEO Tevita Boseiwaqa after fijivillage News raised concerns about the flooding that has again occurred behind MHCC this afternoon.

Boseiwaqa says the Council has already met with the Fiji Roads Authority and Ministry of Waterways to discuss the issue.

There is still no deadline on when this recurring issue will be fixed.

He says the area has an underground outlet issue, while most of the infrastructure is also ageing.

Boseiwaqa says a special drive has been initiated by the Minister for Works to look into the drainage and infrastructure concerns, with the FRA now coming onboard.

The area has experienced repeated flooding during periods of significant rainfall, with the existing drainage infrastructure unable to cope with the volume of water.

We have sent further questions to the Fiji Roads Authority and Waterways for details on the work required and when a permanent solution is expected.
